issue.title: [epic] Make flora condition persistent and texture fallback expressive
issue.body:
## Background

Flora today cannot die of anything but age, and cannot render a state it has no
exact texture for. Verified on master `7680c9ef6`:

- `World.Flora.Types.LifePhaseTag` is one ordered axis holding both
  `PhaseSprout` and `PhaseDead`, so an occurrence cannot be dead *and*
  remembered as a sprout. `World.Flora.Growth.floraGrowth` derives everything
  from placement age, placement-time habitat health, and the world clock and
  writes no per-instance state; habitat health only scales growth and never
  kills. Annuals, biennials, and perennials die only at their lifespan
  boundary, show the authored dead texture for a universal
  `deadWindowDays = 60.0`, then wrap to a new sprout generation. Evergreens
  never die. `lcDeathChance` loads from YAML and is never read.
- `World.Flora.Render.resolveSpeciesTexture` picks one age-driven life phase,
  then one annual stage, with an optional exact `(phase, stage)` override.
  There is no render-context, condition, cause, or phase-at-death axis. A
  declared file missing from disk becomes `unknown_flora.png`, an error
  fallback rather than a semantic fallback to a less specific valid texture.
- Sixteen shipped texture families have juvenile art; none has dead-juvenile
  or cause-specific art. Fourteen have one generic `dead.png`; coconut palm,
  red mangrove, Scots pine, and white spruce have none. Juvenile canvases run
  from 4×4 to 128×128, so one shared dead-sprout bitmap cannot substitute.
- Row crops are ordinary `FloraInstance`s replayed from `WePlaceFlora` /
  `WePlaceFloraWithId` in the `world-edits` component; groundcover crops are
  `CropPlot`s in the tile-keyed per-page map persisted in `world-activity`.
  Neither render input carries an explicit wild/cultivated context, and
  naturally placed flora is deterministic derived chunk content with no
  per-occurrence mutable record. The existing harvest-timer overlay is
  tile-keyed and cannot address several wild occurrences on one tile.
- PR #2136 (closing #1787) landed approved wild and cultivated wheat art under
  `assets/textures/flora/wheat/{wild,cultivated}/`, but `data/flora/crops.yaml`
  still points wheat at white clover because no wild/cultivated selector
  exists. #1688 / PR #1725 landed the base saguaro family (sprout, matured,
  matured_flowering, matured_fruiting, dead) with no dead-juvenile or
  cause-specific art.
- No drought, frost, fire, disease, or damage producer exists anywhere in the
  repository, and no open or closed issue covers persistent flora condition,
  corpse retention, or sparse texture fallback.

## Goal

Any wild or cultivated flora occurrence can carry a persistent semantic
condition, including a death cause and its visual state at the time of death,
and can always resolve a valid texture through one deterministic, documented
sparse fallback system.

The settled contracts are:

- the renderer requests one semantic selector over five axes — context
  (`wild`/`cultivated`), life phase, annual stage, condition (`alive`/`dead`),
  and cause (`natural`, `drought`, `frost`, `fire`, `disease`, `damage`,
  `unknown`) — and the content layer returns a handle plus the fallback
  candidate that won;
- texture variants are sparse, explicitly declared YAML, never discovered by
  filename; a species with only its base texture renders in every
  representable state; fallback drops cultivated to wild, then annual stage,
  then cause, then phase, with death outranking phase outranking cause;
- cultivated art is a presentation override on the one shared lifecycle, not a
  second lifecycle;
- a corpse freezes its life phase and annual stage at death; all persisted
  condition state is semantic and re-resolved after content load — texture
  handles are never saved;
- corpse retention is explicit per-species policy: transient remains expire
  after their window and take exactly one successor (wild reseed or
  cultivated awaiting replanting), while mature structural remains persist
  until cleared; an omitted legacy policy keeps today's 60-day reseed
  behaviour;
- wild occurrences, planted row flora, and groundcover crop plots each have a
  stable identity that survives chunk regeneration and save/load, including
  several occurrences on one tile, keyed by canonical global coordinates;
- existing flora YAML loads unchanged; every new persisted record ships with
  frozen DTOs, an explicit migration, inventory rows, and save-compat coverage;
- art is separately tracked and owner-approved; saguaro is the end-to-end
  pilot, adding only `sprout_dead.png` and a generic `charred.png` so the
  phase-before-cause fallback is exercised by a deliberately missing
  `sprout_charred.png`;
- this arc ships no hazard producer; it ends at a mutation/query seam later
  weather, fire, disease, and damage systems call.

## Phase plan

**Phase 1 — Foundation**

- [ ] **EFM-1:** Publish the canonical flora visual-state and fallback contract — #2530
- [ ] **EFM-2:** Load and audit sparse flora visual and corpse-policy declarations — #2539
- [ ] **EFM-3:** Resolve flora textures through the canonical fallback lattice — #2544

**Phase 2 — Persistence foundation**

- [ ] **EFM-4:** Give flora occurrences stable identity and explicit render context — #2547
- [ ] **EFM-5:** Persist wild and row-flora condition records across regeneration and saves — #2549
- [ ] **EFM-6:** Persist groundcover-crop condition records through the same model — #2552

**Phase 3 — Observable foundation and lifecycle**

- [ ] **EFM-7:** Expose and render persistent flora conditions without hazard producers — #2555
- [ ] **EFM-10:** Apply corpse retention and successor policy — #2557

**Phase 4 — Pilot**

- [ ] **EFM-8:** Create an approved pilot mortality texture set — #2559
- [ ] **EFM-9:** Demonstrate the complete condition and fallback path on one pilot species — #2562

## Dependency structure

EFM-1 is documentation only, depends on nothing, and can land first; it is on
the critical path because every other slice cites it.

EFM-2 depends on EFM-1 and EFM-3 depends on EFM-2: loader vocabulary before
the pure resolver. Both are critical path.

EFM-4 depends on EFM-1 only, so it may proceed in parallel with EFM-2/EFM-3.
EFM-5 depends on EFM-4, and EFM-6 depends on EFM-5. All three are critical
path.

EFM-7 depends on EFM-3, EFM-5, and EFM-6 and joins the two foundation
branches. EFM-10 depends on EFM-7. Both are critical path.

EFM-8 is independent: it is an `art` issue depending only on EFM-1's
filename contract, needs owner preview signoff, and may be worked at any
time after EFM-1. EFM-9 depends on EFM-10 and EFM-8 and closes the arc.

If any child changes worldgen-visible instance identity or output, that child
follows the worldgen-output tier (full headless suite, baselines,
`world_check`, save-version bump). Pure content and schema children do not
claim a world-output change.

## Done when

- One canonical repository section defines the selector axes, vocabulary,
  filename conventions, sparse-declaration rules, fallback order, art tiers,
  and compatibility promises, and flora YAML, loader, resolver, audit, tests,
  and art workflows all reference it.
- Every current flora definition loads unchanged; duplicate or unknown
  selectors and invalid retention/successor combinations fail clearly; every
  repository-owned species declares a valid corpse policy; every declared
  variant path is covered by `tools/texture_subset_audit.py`.
- Table-driven tests prove exact-match, cultivated-to-wild, stage-drop,
  cause-drop, phase-drop, and base fallback order without engine or GPU
  state; a one-texture species always returns its base; a dead sprout never
  resolves adult art when a juvenile fallback exists.
- Condition, cause, context, frozen phase/stage, occurrence identity,
  retention outcome, and expiry survive save/load and component migration for
  wild flora, planted row flora, and groundcover `CropPlot`s, with no texture
  handle in any save.
- Evicting and regenerating a wild chunk leaves the same occurrence dead with
  the same semantic selector; killing one of several occurrences on one tile
  leaves its siblings alive; replanting a crop cannot inherit an old corpse.
- A transient corpse is still dead immediately before expiry, takes its
  successor exactly once at expiry, and does not revive when its overlay is
  removed; persistent remains survive the same elapsed time, eviction, and
  reload.
- The saguaro pilot shows exact dead-juvenile art when present, follows the
  documented fallback for the deliberately omitted charred sprout, retains its
  state through save/load and regeneration, passes a GPU-free probe, and is
  approved by the owner in the real preview.

## Related

- #1688 / PR #1725 (closed) — base saguaro texture family; EFM-8 builds on it.
- #1787 / PR #2136 (closed) — approved wild and cultivated wheat art. Its
  "blocked follow-on integration" items 1–3 (explicit wild/cultivated
  selection, `texDir` subpath acceptance, wild-vs-cultivated request context
  with cultivated-to-wild fallback) are delivered by EFM-2, EFM-3, and EFM-4.
  Pointing the shipped wheat definition at that art, its grain icon, natural
  density, and any retune (items 4–7) remain a separate content-integration
  issue after this arc and are not a child here.
- #2236 (open) — flora species identity by authored name; both children
  (#2241, #2243) are merged. This arc consumes name-keyed species identity and
  adds per-occurrence identity; it does not reopen species identity.
- #332 (closed) — shared derived growth runtime, extended not replaced.
- #334 (closed) — row-crop `FloraInstance`s and groundcover `CropPlot`s, given
  explicit context and condition rather than replaced.
- #1781 (closed) — tomato crop art; tomato mortality art is a later backfill
  candidate, not part of this arc.
- Supporting design record:
  `docs/environmental_flora_mortality_design.md` (not required context for
  implementing individual children).

## Automated cross-agent issue review

Reviewed against `master@704d5ed347e5` by GPT-6-Astra (`gpt-6-astra` at `high`).

**Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED**

Corrections and spec additions below amend the implementation spec. Supporting context is non-normative. Open decisions remain unresolved and must not be guessed.

### Corrections
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Correct the identity premise and bound EFM-4 to extending existing infrastructure: stable wild/planted FloraInstanceId values, canonical-coordinate provenance, persisted planted allocation, and per-instance harvest timers already exist. Preserve those identities and consumers; add the missing context and crop replacement identity. Evidence: src/World/Flora/Identity.hs, src/World/Flora/Harvest.hs, src/World/Flora/CropPlot.hs, and test-headless/Test/Headless/World/FloraIdentity.hs.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Replace the shorthand irreversible axis-dropping description with ordered candidate enumeration: reconsider cultivated then wild at each semantic candidate, and reconsider cause specificity after phase is relaxed. Qualify the juvenile guarantee so juvenile dead art beats generic dead art, while available dead art still outranks living juvenile art. Evidence: the issue's death-before-phase priority and docs/environmental_flora_mortality_design.md, 'Fallback invariants' and 'Proposed fallback shape'.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Correct the legacy duration claim: deadWindowDays is 60 effective growth-days, while floraGrowth advances by growthRate health; at health 0, the dead window spans 240 world days. The omitted-policy compatibility promise must preserve that behavior rather than silently reinterpret it as 60 world days. Evidence: src/World/Flora/Growth.hs, growthRate and floraGrowth.

### Spec additions / clarifications
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Add a fallback regression with living juvenile art and generic dead art but no juvenile dead art, plus a case where cultivated art exists only at a less-specific semantic candidate. These distinguish the intended priorities from plausible incorrect implementations. Grounding: docs/environmental_flora_mortality_design.md, 'Fallback invariants'.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Add non-unit-health coverage for omitted legacy corpse policy, separately from explicit world-day retention policies, to prove the promised compatibility at death and reseed boundaries. Grounding: src/World/Flora/Growth.hs and the issue's omitted-policy compatibility requirement.

### Supporting context
- **GPT-6-Astra:** The checked-out HEAD matches dossier base 704d5ed347e5132eda97ec5d722314e22640cd31. World.Flora.Growth still derives mortality from age, and World.Flora.Render still selects phase/stage textures without persistent condition or cause inputs.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Existing identity coverage includes same-tile siblings, seam aliases, regeneration, allocator persistence, and legacy migration. This makes the identity premise partially stale, not the whole mortality epic unnecessary. Evidence: test-headless/Test/Headless/World/FloraIdentity.hs.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** The requested migration discipline matches src/World/Save/CLAUDE.md: component schema changes require frozen outgoing DTOs and explicit migrations; a global save-version bump cannot substitute for them.

### Open decisions
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Determine whether #2526 is tracking-only and excluded from the one-PR implementation gate, or will be narrowed to one independently deliverable change. Its Phase plan explicitly distributes completion across ten separately numbered children, including documentation, runtime, persistence, art, and integration.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Resolve EFM-8's art delivery granularity: it bundles sprout_dead.png and charred.png into one child, while CLAUDE.md:238 requires each new asset to have its own issue and PR. No owner exception is present in the dossier.

### Recommended disposition
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Retain #2526 as the tracking epic and readiness-review its implementation children individually; apply the premise and fallback corrections to the epic and affected children. Grounding: the issue's explicit Phase plan and dependency structure.
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Split EFM-8 into separately tracked asset deliveries and update EFM-9's prerequisites, or obtain an explicit owner exception permitting the two-image delivery. Grounding: CLAUDE.md:238 and the issue's pilot asset manifest.

### Reviewer summaries
- **GPT-6-Astra — CHANGES REQUESTED:** The mortality and sparse-fallback work is justified, but #2526 is a ten-child tracking epic rather than a one-PR implementation contract. Its art packaging also conflicts with repository rules. Several stale or ambiguous statements can be repaired directly.
